data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact (conn:084384ac0b1e) abstracts from the neighbourhood's source-vs-operational independence distinction by proposing a unifying diagnostic hierarchy: each level of independence evidence (training-history separation, execution-trace presence, injected-false-claim controls) is a strictly increasing test of causal decorrelation, where the covering principle from SRC_005 — that independence is a property of the evidential channel, not the engine boundary — reduces to concrete ablation tests at the run level. The isolated point is that this hierarchy is not a set of alternatives but a cascade: a decorrelated signal (SRC_005) is verified by an operation capable of refutation (SRC_002), which in turn is validated by perturbation sensitivity (SCR_002), and finally confirmed by population statistics with negative controls (SRC_003). The covering principle thus integrates all four positions as progressively stricter levels of the same causal-decorrelation test. This is REFUTED IF any lower-level diagnostic (e.g., single-run perturbation sensitivity without population statistics) can be shown to provide sufficient genuine verification without requiring the higher-level checks — which would mean the levels are alternatives, not a cascade.
